hypothesis: In a fish population surveyed across body sizes, the Fulton-type condition factor K = W/L^3 varies systematically with length (indicating allometric form change during growth) rather than remaining constant, so that k reveals changing form, in most species with continued growth.
pass_criterion: For individual-fish records (length, weight) of at least 10 common DATRAS species with >=1000 weighed fish each, K=W/L^3 is computed per length class. The claim is supported if in >=70% of species log K regresses on log L with slope significantly different from 0 (p<0.01, equivalent to log-log length-weight exponent b deviating from 3 by |b-3|>=0.1), i.e. k varies with length and so flags form change.
fail_criterion: The claim is refuted if in <30% of species |b-3|>=0.1 with p<0.01 (k essentially constant with length), or if k varies but changes in K show no relation to independently recorded shape change (e.g. K trend not linked to length-class), so that k does not discriminate form change.
interpretation: Thompson's k is the Fulton condition factor K = W/L^3 (density and form assumed constant if K is constant). Length is total fish length, weight is individual weight from trawl surveys. Constant K means isometric growth (b=3, unchanged form); variation of K with L means allometry. Modern reinterpretation: K variation can also reflect condition, season, maturity, gonad and stomach content, not only shape, so the test measures only the covariance of k with length (the observable half of the claim). The claim that changes are likely while growth continues is tested via the proportion of species with b significantly different from 3.

dataset.name: DATRAS
dataset.publisher: International Council for the Exploration of the Sea (ICES)
dataset.why_it_fits: Database of Trawl Surveys with raw downloadable survey data (CC BY 4.0) and the icesDATRAS R package; the exchange-format biological (CA) records contain individual fish length and weight (and age) by species, permitting computation of W/L^3 across length classes. Field-level details are in the linked unified format description.
